citations.narrative:
- The licensee has gone over the allowed animal maximum on their USDA license. There were more than 8000 adult and
juvenile animals present at the facility. The licensee is currently licensed for a maximum of 6050 animals.
The USDA license authorizes the maximum number of animals per license. This information helps ensure that all animals
can be adequately housed and cared for.
A licensee must either obtain a new license with an appropriate maximum number of animals or reduce the number of
animals at the facility to below the maximum number of allowed animals.
Correct by 1 November 2026

- In the first housing barn, two long cages housing juveniles had an inadequate number of perches to comfortably house
all the parakeets contained in the enclosures. An enclosure housing perching birds must have a sufficient number of
perches of appropriate size, shape, strength, texture, and placement to comfortably hold all the birds in the primary
enclosure at the same time. A lack of adequate perching space can cause physical and emotional stress to the enclosed
birds and have a negative impact on the welfare of the animals. The facility must ensure that all cages have a sufficient
number of appropriate perches to house all enclosed animals at the same time.
Correct by: 16 September 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
- There was an excessive number of flies present in the interior portion of the first housing barn. Flies were clustered at
different locations throughout the facility, most noticeably on the catch trays underneath bird cages. Flies are an irritant
and a potential source of contamination to the enclosed animals. The facility must institute an appropriate and effective
method of fly and pest control to ensure adequate levels of control and to help protect the health and welfare of the
enclosed animals.
Correct by 16 September 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
CODY YAGER, Avian Field Specialist n
